@@ -139,6 +139,10 @@ When you update to version 2609, existing CMG deployments are automatically migr
 
 Important
 
+Before updating to version 2609, check the vCPU quotas and availability of the new VM sizes in each Azure subscription and region where you deploy a CMG. The VM scale set migration uses a new VM family. Ensure that both the **standard Dadv6 Family vCPUs** quota and the **Total Regional vCPUs** quota have enough available quota for the new instances, with additional headroom for temporary instances during upgrade or maintenance. Quota is the number of vCPUs your subscription is allowed to use. Azure must also have enough resources available in the region to deploy the new VM instances.
+
+Important
+
 Upgrade the Configuration Manager console after updating to version 2609. The updated console is required to display the new CMG VM sizes correctly.
 
 | CMG tier | Previous VM size | Previous vCPU | Previous memory | New VM size | New vCPU | New memory |
@@ -149,6 +153,43 @@ Upgrade the Configuration Manager console after updating to version 2609. The up
 
 Retirement dates are subject to change. For the current retirement date and other VM series retirement details, see [Retired Azure VM size series](/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/lifecycle/retired-sizes-list). VM pricing varies by region. For current pricing, see [Azure Virtual Machines pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/virtual-machines/windows/).
 
+#### Check CMG capacity and vCPU quotas before upgrading
+
+To identify the subscription, region, current VM size, and instance count for each CMG, run the following read-only SQL query against the site database at your top-level site:
+
+```sql
+SELECT Name, Region, SubscriptionId, VmSize, NumberOfInstances
+FROM Azure_Service;
+```
+
+Use the VM size mapping in the preceding table to calculate the required vCPUs for each CMG: multiply the **New vCPU** value by **NumberOfInstances**. Add the requirements for all CMGs in the same subscription and region, account for other workloads that consume these quotas, and allow additional headroom for temporary instances during CMG upgrade or maintenance.
+
+In the Azure portal, check the **standard Dadv6 Family vCPUs** and **Total Regional vCPUs** quotas for each subscription and region identified by the query. Request any necessary increases before upgrading. For instructions, see [Increase regional vCPU quotas - Azure Quotas | Microsoft Learn](/en-us/azure/quotas/regional-quota-requests).
+
+You can also run the following Azure CLI commands from PowerShell to check quota usage and limits. Sign in to Azure CLI first, and replace the placeholders with your subscription ID and Azure region name:
+
+```powershell
+$subscriptionId = '<subscription ID>'
+$region = '<region name>'
+$usage = az vm list-usage --location $region --query "[?name.value=='standardDadv6Family']" --output json --subscription $subscriptionId
+$usage
+
+az vm list-usage --location $region --query "[?name.value=='cores']" --output json --subscription $subscriptionId
+```
+
+If there isn't enough available quota, the CMG migration can fail with a `QuotaExceeded` error in **CloudMgr.log**. For example, the log might include the following details:
+
+```json
+{
+  "details": [
+    {
+      "code": "QuotaExceeded",
+      "message": "Operation could not be completed as it results in exceeding approved Total Regional Cores quota. Additional details - Deployment Model: Resource Manager, Location: <Your location>, Current Limit: 10, Current Usage: 8, Additional Required: 8, (Minimum) New Limit Required: 16."
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
 ## Asset Intelligence
 
 ### Asset Intelligence reports removed

englishSummary.headline: Version 2609 CMG upgrades add vCPU quota checks
englishSummary.summary: The documentation adds pre-upgrade steps for CMG VM scale set migration, including identifying CMGs, calculating required vCPUs, checking standard Dadv6 Family and regional quotas, and requesting increases. Insufficient quota can cause a QuotaExceeded error.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Before upgrading, administrators should verify quota availability for each CMG subscription and region and obtain increases where needed to avoid migration failure.

-- **ADK 10.1.25398.1 (updated September 2023)** Windows PE boot images aren't supported for use with Configuration Manager due to known issues:
+### Note 1: ADK 10.1.26100.x releases
 
-    - VBScript doesn't work in WinPE.
-    - The **Pre-provision BitLocker** task doesn't work in WinPE.
-    - Devices with UFS storage, such as the Surface Go 4, don't work in WinPE.
+All ADK 10.1.26100.x releases (May 2024, December 2024, and September 2026) ship the same Windows PE binaries, **10.1.26100.1**. Only the Deployment Tools were updated between these releases. Earlier releases are no longer available for download. For the current release, see [Download the ADK 10.1.26100.9457 (September 2026)](https://aka.ms/ConfigMgrADKDownload9457).
 
-        Instead use the **ADK 10.1.26100.X (May 2024, Dec 2024)** (10.1.26100.X) or newer where these issues are resolved.

+### Note 2: ADK 10.1.25398.1 Windows PE issues
+
+**ADK 10.1.25398.1 (updated September 2023)** Windows PE boot images aren't supported for use with Configuration Manager due to known issues:
+
+- VBScript doesn't work in WinPE.
+- The **Pre-provision BitLocker** task doesn't work in WinPE.
+- Devices with UFS storage, such as the Surface Go 4, don't work in WinPE.
+
+Instead use **ADK 10.1.26100.x (May 2024, December 2024, September 2026)** where these issues are resolved.
+
+### General guidance
+
+- For information on applying the [BlackLotus UEFI bootkit vulnerability](https://support.microsoft.com/topic/kb5025885-how-to-manage-the-windows-boot-manager-revocations-for-secure-boot-changes-associated-with-cve-2023-24932-41a975df-beb2-40c1-99a3-b3ff139f832d) security updates to boot images from ADKs before **ADK 10.1.26100.1 (May 2024)**, see [Customize Windows PE boot images](/en-us/windows/deployment/customize-boot-image). Boot images from **ADK 10.1.26100.x (May 2024, December 2024, September 2026)** and newer already have the BlackLotus UEFI bootkit vulnerability security update applied to them. For this reason, it's recommended to use boot images from **ADK 10.1.26100.x**.
 - Windows Server builds have the same Windows ADK requirement as the associated Windows client version. For example, Windows Server 2016 is the same build version as Windows 10 LTSB 2016.
 
 - The last supported version of 32-bit WinPE is available in the **WinPE add-on for Windows 10, version 2004** (10.1.19041). Versions of the WinPE add-on for the ADK after the **ADK for Windows 10, version 2004** (10.1.19041) no longer support 32-bit versions of Windows PE (WinPE). For more information, see [Download and install the Windows ADK](/en-us/windows-hardware/get-started/adk-install).

englishSummary.headline: Windows ADK guidance adds the September 2026 release
englishSummary.summary: The support matrix now lists ADK 10.1.26100.9457 as the current September 2026 release and explains that 10.1.26100.x releases share the same Windows PE binaries. englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators can use the updated compatibility guidance when selecting an ADK for Configuration Manager deployments; ADK 10.1.25398.1 remains unsuitable for Windows PE boot images.
